summary: A UAE-focused accounting platform connecting sales, purchases, inventory, banking and ledger-based business reports.
overview: Finora is a business accounting application designed around the daily work of UAE trading and service companies. Sales, purchases, expenses and inventory connect to a double-entry ledger. Teams can review invoices, payments, bank transactions and reports within the same organisation workspace.
detail: The implementation uses Next.js, TypeScript and Prisma, with money stored in integer minor units. The source includes balanced journal posting, reversing entries, document numbering, inventory movements, UAE VAT handling and role-based access. The device mockups were captured from a local build running demonstration data for a fictional trading company; no customer or financial records are shown.
features: Sales invoices, quotes and customer payments
Purchase orders, bills and vendor payments
Bank accounts, transfers and reconciliation
Inventory items, warehouses and valuation
P&L, balance sheet, trial balance and ageing reports
UAE VAT return view, roles and AI assistance
journey: Users move from a customer or supplier record to a commercial document, then to posting and settlement. Every invoice shows the journal entries it created, so staff can trace a balance back to its source. The dashboard summarises cash, receivables and payables and links overdue items to the underlying records.
engineering: Financial documents feed balanced journal entries rather than isolated dashboard totals. The code represents amounts in fils and handles corrections through reversing entries. Tenant context, roles and server-side validation are part of the implementation, alongside reporting, approvals and recurring documents.
delivery: Developed application; not deployed to a public live URL. The documented scope includes accounting, inventory, banking, reports and account administration. The assistant and external services depend on their configured providers. Tax settings and financial reports need business-specific review before operational use; the portfolio does not represent regulatory certification.
next: Finora illustrates a custom business platform built around connected records and traceable transactions. A comparable UAE project starts with the chart of accounts, document lifecycle, approval responsibilities and migration requirements.
steps: Create customer and supplier records with the details needed for documents.
Manage invoices, bills, payments and their posting lifecycle.
Reconcile bank activity and review stock movements across warehouses.
Use ledger-based reports and VAT summaries to understand the business.

summary: A shared workspace for support tickets, tasks, approvals and customer service, with organisation-scoped access and activity history.
overview: Nexora is a help desk and work management application for teams handling service requests alongside everyday tasks. Staff can assign tickets, track status, add internal notes and coordinate project work. Customers have a separate portal, while organisation-level permissions keep each workspace focused on its own records.
detail: Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL, the application connects ticket handling with assets, knowledge articles and approvals. Its source includes authentication, workspace membership, private attachments and scoped API access. The device mockups show the seeded demonstration workspace (fictional users and requests), not a customer account.
features: Ticket assignment and status transitions
Public replies and private internal notes
Project tasks, checklists and time tracking
Customer portal and knowledge articles
SLA targets, assets, departments and locations
Workspace roles, API keys and session management
journey: A request becomes an assigned ticket with a visible status and activity trail. Agents can reply to customers, keep internal context private and link operational work to tasks. Dashboards bring outstanding requests into view so teams can decide what needs attention next.
engineering: Tenant-scoped queries and role checks support separate workspaces. Ticket transitions, attachment access and approval actions follow server-side rules. The interface brings these rules into the daily workflow through status labels, assignment controls and a consistent navigation structure.
delivery: Developed application; not deployed to a public live URL. The implemented scope covers support operations, team tasks and workspace administration. Advanced automation editors, billing checkout and live collaboration are outside the documented completed scope; integrations require their own configuration.
next: Nexora demonstrates how a custom web application can connect service delivery with internal operations. For a similar UAE platform, define staff roles, customer access, ticket states and reporting needs before choosing integrations.
steps: Route incoming requests to the right owner and preserve the conversation history.
Keep task checklists, assignees and tracked time beside project work.
Give customers a dedicated place to follow their support requests.
Control workspace settings, permissions, notifications and knowledge content.

summary: Animated digital invitations with personalisation, guest replies, account-based publishing and event-date access rules.
overview: Invitara is an invitation platform for weddings, engagements, birthdays, baby showers and other celebrations. Customers choose a design, personalise content and share a published guest link. The product combines animated storytelling with an editor, RSVP collection and an account dashboard.
detail: The application uses Node.js, Express, SQLite and locally bundled animation libraries (GSAP, Motion, Anime.js and Three.js). The current collection contains independently designed invitations across many occasions, each built on a shared editor and content contract. Couple names and event details in the mockups are template placeholders, not commissioned client events.
features: Independently designed invitation compositions
Editable content, images, theme and section order
Guest replies and CSV export
Account-based saves and publishing
Stripe webhook purchase verification
Timezone-aware event expiry
journey: A visitor previews a theme and creates a personalised draft before purchase. Verified checkout unlocks the purchased experience. The owner can publish a guest link, collect replies and review responses, with editing access governed by the selected event date and timezone.
engineering: The server checks purchase status and expiry for save and publish actions. Stripe redirects alone do not unlock a purchase: the application verifies signed webhook events. Password hashing, account sessions and private owner access protect the editing and RSVP workflows.
delivery: Developed application; not deployed to a public live URL. Drafts and previews work without payment credentials. Live checkout requires configured Stripe keys and webhook delivery. After the event, the editor becomes read-only and replies close while the published invitation remains available as a keepsake.
next: Invitara connects expressive web design with a practical content and purchase workflow. A similar event product should define who can edit, how guests respond, when access expires and what remains available after the event.
steps: Preview themes with distinct typography, motion and opening interactions.
Personalise text, photos, colours and section order in the editor.
Publish after verified purchase and share the invitation with guests.
Manage guest replies and retain the invitation after the event ends.

summary: An industrial catalogue website connecting UAE buyers with product specifications, sector information and quotation enquiries.
overview: Mechaura International is an industrial supplier website organised around products, sectors and quotation enquiries. Its catalogue covers abrasive brushes, bearings, hydraulic hoses and pumps, filtration, cutting tools and elevator accessories. Product imagery and motion content help buyers understand the range before contacting the supplier.
detail: The project uses a Vite build with generated product, sector, location and article pages, a sitemap and llms.txt workflow and optimised image assets. A companion WordPress theme packages the same design for WordPress hosting. The device mockups are captured from the production build of the website.
features: Product-led catalogue navigation and part-number search
Dedicated product family pages with specifications
Sector and Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah landing pages
Multi-step quotation and WhatsApp enquiry journeys
Technical guides for maintenance teams
Optimised WebP imagery, structured data and sitemap
journey: Buyers can enter through search, a product category, an industry or a city page, review relevant equipment and move to a quotation enquiry. The website separates product information from company and service content so technical and commercial visitors can find an appropriate next step.
engineering: Product and editorial pages are generated as static content for delivery through the website build. Images are prepared in WebP, while videos provide supporting product context. Metadata, structured data and sitemap generation keep discovery tied to the pages that the build actually publishes.
delivery: The delivered website scope is catalogue presentation and business enquiries. It is not presented as an online checkout or stock-control application. Product availability, quotation responses and fulfilment remain supplier-operated processes.
next: Mechaura shows how an industrial website can organise technical products for UAE and GCC buyers. A similar catalogue starts with product categories, usable specifications, sector requirements and a clear enquiry route.
steps: Organise the catalogue around equipment categories and buyer terminology.
Explain product applications through dedicated pages and original visuals.
Connect industry and city content with relevant products and enquiry actions.
Generate static pages, optimise assets and publish a crawlable sitemap.

summary: An internal tool that turns incoming emails into owned tasks, drafts professional replies and chases work until it is closed.
overview: WorkFlow Hub is built around a common operations loop: a request arrives by email, someone reads it, assigns it, replies and follows up until it is done. It covers website, online payments, web development, store support and back-office categories. Each task has a single owner, a due date and an activity history.
detail: The application uses Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL with session-based sign-in for administrators and employees. An AI step extracts the subject, sender, summary, category and priority from a pasted email and drafts an editable reply. The device mockups were captured from a local build running demonstration data; names, branches and tasks are fictional.
features: Email-to-task intake with AI summary and reply draft
Kanban board and filterable list views
Single-owner assignment with comments and activity log
Automatic reminders, overdue flags and follow-up cadence
Domain, hosting and contract renewal tracking
Departments, branches, reports and notifications
journey: An administrator pastes an email, reviews the extracted details and the suggested reply, then creates the task and assigns an employee. The assignee is notified, updates status on the board and adds comments. The follow-up engine reminds owners before due dates and flags work that stalls.
engineering: Scheduled jobs evaluate due dates, review reminders and renewal windows against configurable thresholds. Status changes write activity logs and notifications. Role checks separate administrator screens such as employees, settings and reports from the employee workspace.
delivery: Developed internal application. Outlook mailbox integration and AI drafting depend on configured providers; drafts are always reviewed before a reply is sent from the user's own mail client.
next: WorkFlow Hub shows how a focused internal tool can replace scattered email threads and spreadsheets. A similar project starts with the real request sources, the categories of work and the follow-up rules the team already uses.
steps: Capture incoming requests and summarise them into structured tasks.
Assign one clear owner, a priority and a due date.
Track progress on the board and keep context in comments.
Let reminders, renewals and reports keep work moving to completion.

summary: A property and lease platform managing plots, units, subtenants, subleases, EJARI registrations, rent collection and compliance alerts.
overview: The system manages the full hierarchy from landlord to internal tenant company, property and plot, unit or warehouse, subtenant and EJARI registration. Property managers track main leases and subleases, finance users follow invoices and receipts, and the dashboard summarises occupancy, contract value and upcoming expiries.
detail: Built with Next.js 16, TypeScript, Prisma, Zustand and Recharts, with role-based access for super administrators, property managers, finance users and read-only viewers. The data model was designed from the client's lease spreadsheet. All company names, contract numbers, plot numbers and amounts in the mockups were replaced with fictional demonstration values.
features: Companies, properties, plots and unit registers
Main lease and sublease contracts with fee calculations
Subtenant records with trade licence tracking
EJARI registration status and expiry tracking
Rent collection with invoices and receipts
Compliance alerts, reports and role-based access
journey: A manager opens the dashboard, sees occupancy and leases approaching expiry, then drills into a property, its units and the subleases attached to them. Compliance alerts point to contracts, EJARI registrations or licences that need action, and reports export the data for review.
engineering: Each level of the hierarchy is a related record, so totals on the dashboard come from the same data the registers display. Expiry checks generate compliance alerts, and an audit log records changes. Role checks limit editing to the appropriate users.
delivery: Developed application for a property management client. Data import from the client's spreadsheets is part of the build; publication of client-identifying details requires the client's approval.
next: This project shows how a lease spreadsheet can become a structured operational system. A similar platform starts with the ownership hierarchy, contract types, renewal rules and the regulatory registrations the team must track.
steps: Model the portfolio from landlord and company down to units and subtenants.
Record leases and subleases with values, dates and EJARI references.
Track rent invoices, receipts and outstanding balances.
Surface expiries and compliance actions before they become problems.

alt: CertGuard dashboard on laptop, tablet and phone — domains, certificates, servers and alerts
CertGuard domain list with registrar, SSL expiry, domain expiry and verification status
CertGuard domain detail comparing stored dates with RDAP and live SSL results
CertGuard certificate inventory with issuer, validity and install status

summary: A domain and SSL control panel that verifies expiry dates against live sources, alerts before expiry and automates certificate renewal.
overview: CertGuard centralises domains, SSL/TLS certificates, servers and DNS providers for teams that manage many websites. Instead of trusting manually entered dates, it checks domain registration data and inspects the certificate served by each site, then flags mismatches, upcoming expiries and errors.
detail: The application uses Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma and PostgreSQL. Domain expiry comes from RDAP, certificates are inspected over a live TLS connection, and issuance follows an ACME workflow with HTTP-01 or DNS-01 validation. The mockups use the built-in demonstration data (example.com-style domains).
features: RDAP domain verification and live SSL inspection
Stored-versus-discovered date comparison
ACME certificate request, renewal and rollback
SSH server registry with Nginx and Apache operations
Email, WhatsApp, Telegram and Slack alerts
Automation logs, reports and role-based access
journey: An administrator adds a domain; CertGuard verifies registration and certificate details and marks the record as verified or mismatched. The dashboard and notifications highlight what expires soon, and renewals can be requested, installed and verified with every step recorded.
engineering: Verification, issuance and installation are separate services behind interfaces, so providers can be swapped. Credentials and tokens are stored encrypted, deployments validate configuration before reload and roll back on failure, and every operation writes an audit entry.
delivery: Developed application. Live certificate issuance and installation require configured ACME, DNS and SSH access; without them the issuance pipeline runs in a clearly marked simulation mode.
next: CertGuard reflects the day-to-day work of keeping dozens of domains and certificates healthy. A similar tool starts with an inventory of domains, registrars, hosting servers and who must be notified before something expires.
steps: Add domains and verify their registration and SSL details.
Compare stored dates with authoritative sources and resolve mismatches.
Request, renew and install certificates with logged automation.
Alert the right people well before any expiry date.
